item.title: Group Actions on Aspherical Alexandrov Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.32081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conner and Raymond proved that if a connected, compact Lie group $G$ acts effectively on a closed aspherical manifold $M$, then $G$ is a torus and the fundamental group of $G$ injects into the center of $\pi_1(M)$. We prove the corresponding result for effective isometric actions on closed, aspherical Alexandrov spaces.
item.dc:creator: No\'e B\'arcenas, Jes\'us N\'u\~nez-Zimbr\'on

item.title: Sobolev inequalities for sections and projections of log-concave functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Higher order sharp Sobolev and local Sobolev type inequalities for log-concave functions are established. The new inequalities directly imply the isoperimetric inequalities by Bollob\'as and Thomason in 1995, by Liakopoulos in 2019, and the recently discovered local isoperimetric inequalities from [1]. In order to do so, we make use of three ingredients. First, sets of functional inequalities proven by Alonso-Guti\'errez, Bernu\'es, Brazitikos and Carbery in 2021. Second, a multidimensional polynomial optimization result that originated in [1] and was initiated by Bollob\'as and Thomason. Third, a new integral formula for the projection of a log-concave function that links the geometric part with the more functional versions via some dependence on the Hessian matrix restricted to subspaces.
item.dc:creator: Luis J. Al\'ias, Bernardo Gonz\'alez Merino, Beatriz Mar\'in Gimeno

item.title: The Pu inequality and the Viterbo conjecture with finite symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.31906v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a construction for producing Finsler metrics on the sphere from convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^4$ using the quaternions. Among several applications, we prove the weak Viterbo conjecture for convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^4$ that are invariant under the natural action of the quaternion group $Q$. This is the first instance where Viterbo's systolic inequality is established for convex bodies with a finite group symmetry, addressing a question of Haim-Kislev-Ostrover. Moreover, a smooth $Q$-symmetric convex domain that achieves equality is symplectomorphic to the ball, without any assumption of strict or uniform convexity. Finally, we show that any link of minimal Reeb orbits on the boundary of a uniformly convex $Q$-symmetric convex body is transversely isotopic to a union of Hopf fibers, strengthening a result of Abbondandolo-Edtmair-Kang in the $Q$-symmetric setting.
item.dc:creator: Julian Chaidez, Shira Tanny

item.title: The number of Tverberg partitions beyond prime powers
item.description: arXiv:2610.32086v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sierksma's conjecture asserts that every affine map $a\colon\Delta_{(d+1)(r-1)}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^d$ has at least $((r-1)!)^d$ unordered Tverberg partitions into $r$ parts. Until now, lower bounds growing with $d$ were known only when $r$ is a prime power. As one of our main results we prove that for every integer $r\geq3$, every decomposition $r=kq+s$ into $q=p^\alpha$ a prime power, $k\geq1$ and $s\geq0$, and every affine map $a$, the number $\operatorname{Tv}(a)$ of unordered Tverberg partitions satisfies \[ \operatorname{Tv}(a)\ \geq\ \frac{q}{r!}\,\Big(\frac{q}{\alpha+1}\Big)^{\big\lceil\frac{(r-1-2s)(d+1)}{2}\big\rceil}. \]
item.dc:creator: Matija Blagojevi\'c, Pavle V. M. Blagojevi\'c

item.title: A Linear Lower Bound for Convex Body Chasing in Every $\ell_p$ Norm
item.description: arXiv:2610.32670v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish an $\Omega(d)$ lower bound on the competitive ratio of convex body chasing in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $\ell_p$ movement costs for any $p \in [1, \infty)$. Previously, the best known lower bound for general $p$ was $\Omega(\max\{\sqrt{d}, d^{1-1/p}\})$, established by Bubeck et al. (2019); a linear lower bound was known only for $p = \infty$, realized by the standard construction of chasing faces of a hypercube. Our lower bound strictly improves on the prior bound for every fixed $p \in [1, \infty)$ and shows that the functional Steiner point algorithm of Sellke (2023) - which has competitive ratio $O(d)$ - is asymptotically optimal for every $\ell_p$ norm. Our lower bound is based on the recursive construction of Bubeck, Coester, and Rabani (2023) for metrical service systems, which gives a lower bound of $\Omega(r^2)$ for requests of size $O(r)$ in that setting. We show that requests in their construction, each comprising a set of discrete points in a graph metric, can be mapped to the vertices of convex requests in a $(2r+1)$-dimensional vector space while approximately preserving movement costs up to a factor of $O(r)$, which establishes the lower bound.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Christianson

item.title: A new lower bound for the kissing number in 19 dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2603.10425v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the kissing number in 19 dimensions is at least 11948, improving the bound of Cohn and Li by 256. Their odd-sign construction reduces the problem to finding a binary code of length 19 and minimum distance 5 inside a 5-punctured extended binary Golay code. In an explicit model $D$ of this ambient code, the 21 words of weights 3 and 4 are exactly the pairwise differences that such a code must avoid. They span a 10-dimensional subcode $K$. We exhibit a 6-dimensional subcode $M\le K$ for which all 21 words lie in only five cosets of $M$. After identifying $K/M$ with $\mathbb F_2^4$, these five cosets are represented by $\Sigma=\{e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4,e_1+e_2+e_3+e_4\}$. In the graph on $\mathbb F_2^4$ in which $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when $u+v\in\Sigma$, the set $\Sigma$ itself is independent. Lifting its five vertices gives 320 words in $K$, and translating this set through the four cosets of $K$ in $D$ gives a nonlinear code of size 1280 and minimum distance 5.
item.dc:creator: Boon Suan Ho

item.title: A unified approach to Penner, Ptolemy, and Casey's theorems in several dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2605.23430v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove Penner's theorem on horocycles and theorems of Ptolemy and Casey, all with full converses, in hyperbolic space of several dimensions. Recently Waddle observed that the equations underpinning these three theorems are related, and it is this viewpoint that we advance, using the Lorentzian model of hyperbolic space. We show that all three theorems can be derived from a common Gram-matrix calculation applied to lightlike, timelike, and spacelike vectors. Remarkably, our approach gives a version of Casey's theorem in the plane with a full converse, involving three geometric alternatives, which to our knowledge has not previously been recorded.
item.dc:creator: Isabella Lewis, Ian Short

item.title: Strongly log-concave measures and lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.29238v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Lambda \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full rank lattice with the property that $\det \Gamma \ge 1$ for all sublattices $\Gamma \subseteq \Lambda^*$. We prove that there exists a symmetric random vector $X \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with a smooth, strictly positive density $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to (0, \infty)$ satisfying that (1) $f$ is $\alpha$-strongly log-concave, where $\alpha = 2\pi/e$, and (2) $X + \Lambda$ is uniform on $\mathbb{R}^n/\Lambda$. Moreover, the existence of such a density characterizes this property up to a universal dilation. There are a few consequences of the above. We list some. First, for such lattices we can bound the covering radius \[ \mu(\Lambda, K) = \max_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\min_{\lambda\in\Lambda} \left\|x-\lambda\right\|_K \le \sqrt{\frac{2e}{\pi}} \cdot \mathbb{E}\,\left\|G\right\|_K \] of a convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ containing $0$ in its interior, where $G \sim N(0,\mathrm{Id})$. This implies an $O(n \sqrt{\log n})$ bound for the flatness constant and an $O(\log^{3/2} n)$ bound for the subspace flatness constant. We also compare the entire ordered spectrum of the associated flat torus on $\Lambda^*$ with that of a Gaussian, yielding an alternative proof of the reverse Minkowski theorem.
item.dc:creator: Brayden Letwin, Victor Reis, Thomas Rothvoss

item.title: Affine fractional Orlicz--Sobolev inequalities and optimal star bodies
item.description: arXiv:2610.30689v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish an affine fractional Orlicz--Sobolev inequality by replacing the Euclidean fractional Orlicz seminorm with an energy obtained by minimizing over origin-symmetric star bodies of prescribed volume. Under finite lower and upper power growth assumptions, a subcritical upper growth bound, and a monotonicity condition on $t^{n/s+2}\Phi''(t)$, the resulting inequality has the same best constant as its Euclidean counterpart. The power case recovers the affine fractional Sobolev inequality of Haddad and Ludwig with the corresponding Luxemburg normalization. To establish this inequality, we investigate the underlying geometric extremal problem. For every nonzero smooth function of compact support, the existence and uniqueness of an optimal star body are proved under the growth assumptions alone, and its radial function is characterized by an equation involving $\Phi(t)+(s/n)t\Phi'(t)$. We also establish an anisotropic rearrangement inequality, together with its equality conditions under additional strictness assumptions. Moreover, the normalized local limit is investigated. The optimized energies converge to the local energy, and the radial functions of the minimizing bodies converge uniformly on the sphere. The limiting modular is determined by $\overline\Phi(t)=\int_0^t\Phi(\tau)\,d\tau/\tau$. Finally, we compare optimization over star bodies with optimization in the affine orbit.
item.dc:creator: Ai-Jun Li, Qingzhong Huang

item.title: Simple Tilings of Riemannian Homogeneous Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2402.10194v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We define simple tilings in the general context of a $G$-tiling on a Riemannian homogeneous space $M$ to be tilings by Riemannian simplices. As evidence that this definition is natural, we prove that a large class of tilings of $M$ are MLD to simple ones. We further show that there is an isomorphism between \u{C}ech cohomology and pattern-equivariant cohomology of simple tilings of homogeneous Riemannian Spaces. This demonstrates the utility of our definition by generalizing an established result on the topology of tiling spaces of Euclidean space.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Hansen

item.title: Counterexamples to a dimension-free variant of Erd\H{o}s's diameter conjecture for separated distances
item.description: arXiv:2604.15305v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Erd\H{o}s asked about the least possible diameter of an $n$-point set in Euclidean space when any two pairwise distances differ by at least $1$. We consider the uniform-in-dimension variant of his question, in which the dimension $d$ may grow with $n$ and the error term is independent of $d$, and answer it in the negative by an explicit construction. For every prime power $q$, we construct a set $\mathcal X_n$ of $n=q+1$ points in $\mathbb R^{q^2+q}=\mathbb R^{n^2-n}$ such that the $\binom{n}{2}$ pairwise distances are mutually at least $1$ apart, yet $$\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal X_n)\le \Bigl(1-\frac{1}{\pi^2}+o(1)\Bigr)n^2.$$ The construction combines a Singer cyclic difference set with a weighted product of $N=\binom n2$ regular $m$-gons, where $m=q^2+q+1$. The weights are chosen so that the resulting distances increase while the gaps between consecutive distances decrease. After normalizing the smallest gap to $1$, all distinct pairwise distances are separated by at least $1$, while the diameter has asymptotic constant $1-1/\pi^2<1$.
item.dc:creator: Boon Suan Ho

item.title: A $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebraic Hoffman-Wielandt theorem
item.description: arXiv:2605.22585v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We observe that the $2$-norm distance $d_{U,2}$ between the unitary orbits of normal elements in a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $\mathcal{M}$ is equal to the $2$-Wasserstein distance between the spectral measures induced by the trace $\tau_\mathcal{M}$. Using classification and optimal transport theory, we deduce an analogous $2$-norm equation for normal operators $x$ and $y$ in simple, separable, unital, nuclear, $\mathcal{Z}$-stable $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebras that are either monotracial, or real rank zero with finitely many extremal traces, provided that $\sigma(x)=\sigma(y)$ is convex. Consequently, $d_{U,2}$ equips the set of approximate unitary equivalence classes of contractive normal elements of $\mathcal{M}$ with the structure of a compact length space. The same is true of the set of equivalence classes of embeddings into the Jiang-Su algebra $\mathcal{Z}$ of classifiable tracial $2$-Wasserstein spaces over compact, convex planar domains.
item.dc:creator: Bhishan Jacelon

item.title: Exact Reachability under Vertex- and Area-Centroid Control
item.description: arXiv:2607.22981v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A vertex-centroid move slides one vertex of a polygon along the line through it and the centroid of all vertices; Problem 60 of The Open Problems Project asks whether such moves can make every polygon regular. We prove that two simple labeled $n$-gons, with straight angles allowed, are joined through simple polygons by finitely many positive moves exactly when they have the same orientation; a nonconstant move is positive if the vertex remains on the same side of the centroid of the other vertices. The same holds for flows toward or away from the instantaneous area centroid. Inward-only or outward-only moves reach every target of the same orientation up to translation and positive scaling. The common mechanism is a first-order criterion: a symmetric definite center response makes the one-vertex fields of a smooth affine-equivariant center bracket generating. The response is a weighted covariance for point barycenters and $(d+2)$ times the volume covariance for polyhedral centroids. Once translation and scale are factored out, the fields sum to zero, giving exact one-sided control. We resolve Problem 60 under both conventions for a vertex at the centroid. For the vertex-centroid system on $n$ affinely spanning points in $\mathbb{R}^d$, we classify positive-move reachability and prove a local $3dn$-move bound.
item.dc:creator: Yongjie Guan

item.title: Explicit second moments of symplectic Siegel transforms
item.description: arXiv:2610.03499v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give two alternate formulations for the second moment formula of the Siegel transform over $\mathrm{Sp}(2n, \mathbb Z) \backslash \mathrm{Sp}(2n,\mathbb R)$, previously established by Athreya-Konstantoulas and Kelmer-Yu. We also provide several applications that demonstrate their usefulness.
item.dc:creator: Kristian Holm, Seungki Kim
